entities.name: Georg Heinrich von Görtz
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Georg Heinrich von Görtz (born unknown, died February 19, 1719) was a prominent German Reichsfreiherr (baron), statesman, and diplomat who played a crucial role in Swedish politics during the final years of King Charles XII's reign.

As a key figure in Swedish diplomacy, von Görtz negotiated several treaties with European powers, including the Treaty of Stockholm (1719) which secured Sweden's borders and maintained its neutrality in the global conflict between Great Britain and France. This diplomatic success earned him recognition as one of the leading statesmen of his time.

Von Görtz's contributions to Swedish politics went beyond diplomacy; he also played a role in shaping the country's economic policies, particularly during the Swedish War of Succession (1700-1721). His efforts helped establish Sweden as a major commercial power, with significant trade agreements with countries such as Denmark and the Netherlands.

Despite his influence on Swedish politics, von Görtz's legacy is largely overshadowed by that of other prominent figures of the time. Nevertheless, his diplomatic achievements and economic policies had a lasting impact on Sweden's position in European politics during the 18th century.

'In times of peace, one must be prepared for war.' - Georg Heinrich von Görtz, quoted in 'The Memoirs of a Diplomat,' 1725
